details:
Q1: The implementer will rebuild group 3 / shard 1 (4 groups × 4 shards) from the remaining-tests list and run that slice of `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`. If a test fails, it fixes the failing assertion or the poller defect. What should happen if the slice passes, meaning the failure looks like a one-off?
Choices:
A. Make no code change. Report it as a failure that did not reproduce, with the slice's test list and the passing result, so the issue can close. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Harden whichever tests in that slice look timing- or environment-sensitive (for example, sandbox temp dirs or subprocess timeouts), even without a confirmed failure.
C. Stop and hand the issue to a human (`ai:needs-human`) without changing code.
Q2: The triage was inconclusive because the CI annotations only say `shard N failed (exit 1)`. The failing test's name is only in the collapsed per-shard log. Should this fix also change the shard loop in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` so that each failing shard prints its `FAIL`/error lines as `::error::` annotations? The pass/fail gate would stay the same.
Choices:
A. No. Limit the change to the test or poller defect found under Q1. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Yes. Also print the failing test names from failed shards as annotations in the orchestrate-poll step, and update `tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py` to match. **Note:** this edits an automation path (`.github/workflows/`), so the issue needs a `files_touched` entry for it, or the implement guard will reject the commit.
